title: api gateway: routing rules, streaming proxy buffer tuning, and payload size limits to improve streaming stability and OpenAI-compat behavior
author: Priya Menon
description: Motivation: intermittent streaming stalls and tool/function-calling failures were observed when requests routed across internal proxy boundaries and when large structured outputs were produced. This PR tightens routing rules, increases streaming proxy buffers, and enforces more explicit payload-size/splitting behavior to reduce head-of-line blocking and improve OpenAI-compat edge cases. What changed: 1) Routing: added a routing policy predicate that pins streaming sessions to the same proxy pool for the lifetime of the request when the session requests function/tool calling or structured output. This avoids re-routing mid-stream which caused partial event loss. 2) Streaming proxy buffers: increased in-memory streaming buffers and added backpressure signals between proxy and runtime so slow consumer behavior no longer stalls unrelated connections. 3) Payload size limits and splitting: added a deterministic splitting step for large structured outputs (arrays/JSON) emitted by models to keep proxy payload frames under 4MB; SDKs updated to reassemble frames transparently. 4) OpenAI compatibility: updated the OpenAI-compat adapter to preserve event ordering for function_call and tool_call events and to translate Redwood structured-output framing to the OpenAI streaming framing when compatibility mode is enabled. 5) Telemetry: added metrics for streaming_latency_p95, streaming_rebuffers, routing_reassignments, and structured_frame_drops; dashboards updated. Rollout plan: staged rollout by region: start with us-west-2 -> us-east-1 -> eu-west-1 with a 1% traffic canary, monitor streaming_rebuffers and API error rate for 6h, then ramp gradually. Checklist: - [x] unit tests for routing predicate and buffer backpressure - [x] integration e2e streaming test against OpenAI-compat adapter - [x] SDK TS/Python frame reassembly tests - [x] docs and migration notes added - [x] canary rollout plan documented Breaking changes: none expected; behavior is opt-out via feature flag for private instances. Impact on customers: improves streaming stability for long-running tool/function calls and reduces incidents caused by mid-stream reassignments; small latency increase (0-2ms median) in some short non-stream requests due to routing affinity checks. See release_notes for details.

release_notes: API Gateway: improved streaming stability and OpenAI-compat behavior by enforcing routing affinity for streaming sessions (avoids mid-stream reassignments), tuning proxy streaming buffers and backpressure, and adding deterministic splitting/reassembly for large structured outputs to keep frames under 4MB. No breaking changes by default; feature-flagged for private deployments. Recommend SDK patch release (TS/Python) to pick up reassembly fixes.
notes_for_ops: Rollout: use deploy/rollout/canary_streaming.sh to apply changes per region. Monitor metrics: streaming_rebuffers, streaming_latency_p95, routing_reassignments, api_error_rate. If streaming_rebuffers spikes > 3x baseline, rollback immediately. Feature-flag: FEATURE_STREAM_AFFINITY controls affinity behavior for private installs.
